data_source: Week 2 SQLite sales table, daily units sold by date/store/item; weekly aggregation Monday-start.
historical_period: 2013-01-07 through 2017-12-25 (260 complete weeks; opening partial week excluded)
forecast_method: Seasonal naive: future week uses observed demand from 52 weeks earlier, consistent with Week 4 selected global baseline.
week5_formula: Safety stock = z * sample standard deviation of weekly demand * sqrt(assumed lead time); ROP = average weekly demand * assumed lead time + safety stock.
week6_formula: Safety stock = z * standard deviation of historical seasonal-naive residuals * sqrt(protection period); ROP = future forecast for assumed lead time + lead-time safety stock; order-up-to = forecast over lead time + review period + protection-period buffer.
important_limitations: Default lead time and review period are illustrative assumptions, not measurements.
The baseline assumes a normal approximation and independent week-level forecast errors for the square-root buffer.
Sales are used as a proxy for demand, but lost sales during stockouts are not observed.
Policy simulation is a what-if backtest on the final 13 historical weeks, not a real deployment result.
Inventory position upload is needed to turn reorder thresholds into live reorder alerts.
